Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(X<x)=P(Z<\frac{x-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =0$ and $\sigma =10.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-11.7) & =P(Z<\frac{-11.7-0}{10}) \\  & =P(Z<-1.17) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.17) \\  & =Φ(-1.17)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/9b47010de67e748c75465b0ad1ec54d984ec7eaac6721ae9fb9b11cb60c16b16.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(-1.17)=0.1210.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X<-11.7)=0.1210.
$$
